tagline: The AI first responder for insurance claims intake.

scenes.title: The call is the claim.
scenes.narration: A driver crashes, calls, and talks to Ivy. She checks they're safe, takes the policy number, and files the claim while they're still on the line.

scenes.title: One call, start to finish
scenes.narration: Ivy runs on AssemblyAI's voice agent platform. Before she says anything about a policy, she verifies who's calling — and a wrong answer gets the exact same response whether that policy is real or not. Drivability only ever comes from what the caller says out loud, never inferred from how they describe the damage.

code: four required fields only              → tool.call fires
+ caller_name (copied from the caller)  → tool.call fires
+ severity (an enum it picks from)      → tool.call fires
+ description ("in your own words")     → NEVER FIRES
scenes.eyebrow: THE ONE API GOTCHA THAT BIT
scenes.title: A field the model can't compose kills the tool
scenes.narration: Bisected against the live API, one property at a time. Four required fields, it fires. Add a copied field, still fires. Ask it to compose one sentence in its own words, and the tool call never fires again — no error, Ivy just says she's filing it, forever.

scenes.title: Scored and triaged as it's filed
scenes.narration: The moment Ivy files a claim, it lands here — risk score, drivability, and whether a tow is on the way, before the caller has even hung up.

scenes.title: The recording, not just the summary
scenes.narration: Every call is transcribed and recorded in stereo — the caller on one channel, Ivy on the other — so a dispatcher can hear exactly what was said, not just what got typed.

scenes.title: The call after the call
scenes.narration: When a car isn't drivable, a second agent rings recovery operators, ranked by distance, and updates the board the moment one accepts.

scenes.title: Where Ivy needs to get better
scenes.narration: Not just what happened — how the agent is doing. Which question she needs a second attempt on, most often, is the one to fix in the prompt next.

scenes.title: The book Ivy verifies against
scenes.narration: Every policyholder she can check a caller against, in one place — so a wrong answer gets refused the same way whether the policy is real or not.

scenes.title: A link, texted, that stays live
scenes.narration: The caller gets a link back — their claim, their tow's ETA, a place to drop a photo from the roadside — updating in real time as the dispatcher works it.

scenes.title: Ivy's whole personality, one prompt
scenes.narration: Voice, tone, and turn-taking are all editable from here — publish a change and it's live on the next call, no redeploy required.

scenes.title: Press Start. Say what happened.
scenes.narration: One app serves the call, the board, and the dispatcher — no separate systems to keep in sync. That's ClaimVoice.
